items.statement: The adjacent complete statements, assumptions and formula proofs describe the exact generic results; the optional Lean is initially folded.
assumptions: E has finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel structures. P is a true joint probability with standard Gaussian first marginal.
N>0. Only the two selected lists of feature slices are assumed to be in L²(Pₓ); global kernel measurability, a uniform feature bound, and nonsampled feature moments are not assumed.
W and X are measurable, and singletons in W are measurable. P is an actual joint probability; its response coordinate is in L²(P).
W is measurable; H is a complete real inner-product normed space.
p is any finite real polynomial, and the actual second-coordinate response belongs to L²(P). Input and response need not be independent.
μ and ν are probabilities. Φ is genuinely Bochner integrable under each; y is any vector in H.

formulae.label: Differentiating a quadratic risk along a probability segment
A finite empirical segment has the actual joint-risk derivative
An actual Gaussian joint-data risk has a first variation

obligations.label: Differentiating a quadratic risk along a probability segment

bindings.boundary: This is a genuine probability-segment theorem for an H-valued feature mean. An actual scalar data-risk formula still requires a separate averaging identity.; The derivative is within [0,1] at zero. No two-sided derivative of the clipped positive-measure extension is asserted.

assumption_deltas.source: Let μ and ν be probability measures on a measurable parameter space W. Let Φ map W to a real Hilbert space H and be Bochner integrable under both laws, and let y be a fixed vector in H. Write m(ρ)=∫Φ dρ, R(ρ)=‖m(ρ)−y‖², and V(w)=2⟨m(μ)−y,Φ(w)⟩. For every 0≤t≤1, the actual positive measure ρₜ=(1−t)μ+tν is a probability, Φ is integrable under ρₜ, and its mean is the affine interpolation of the endpoint means. V is integrable under both endpoint laws. The right derivative of R(ρₜ) at zero is ∫V dν−∫V dμ. The exact remainder R(ν)−R(μ)−(∫V dν−∫V dμ) is ‖m(ν)−m(μ)‖², and is therefore nonnegative.

bindings.boundary: No independence or product decomposition of P is used.; At parameters outside both finite supports the inner potential integral is only the totalized formula unless additional integrability is proved. This finite-law theorem does not assert an arbitrary-law global first variation.

assumption_deltas.source: Let P be a probability law on X×ℝ, with its actual input marginal Pₓ. Let K:W×X→ℝ be a scalar feature, and assume the actual response coordinate belongs to L²(P). Choose N>0 and two indexed parameter configurations w₀,w₁ of length N. Assume only their selected feature functions K(wₐʲ,·) belong to L²(Pₓ), for a=0,1 and every index j. Let ρ₀ and ρ₁ be their literal equally weighted Dirac empirical measures, retaining repeated indices. Define fρ(x)=∫K(w,x) dρ(w), F(ρ)=∫(fρ(x)−y)² dP(x,y), and V(w)=2∫(fρ₀(x)−y)K(w,x) dP(x,y). Every mixture (1−t)ρ₀+tρ₁ for 0≤t≤1 is a probability with integrable squared loss. V is integrable under both empirical laws, and the actual scalar risk along the mixture has right derivative ∫V dρ₁−∫V dρ₀ at zero.

No pointwise identification with an unspecified preselected first variation is asserted.; The derivative is within the probability interval. Spatial gradient bounds, Wasserstein regularity, stochastic dynamics and statistical convergence are separate results.

assumption_deltas.source: Let P be an actual probability law on E×ℝ, where E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure. Assume only that its input marginal is the standard Gaussian and its actual response coordinate Y is square-integrable. Let p be any finite real polynomial. For any probability ρ on the unit sphere define fρ(x)=∫p(⟨w,x⟩) dρ(w), F(ρ)=∫(fρ(x)−y)² dP(x,y), and Vρ(w)=2∫(fρ(x)−y)p(⟨w,x⟩) dP(x,y). Every squared loss is integrable, and every displayed inner residual-feature product is integrable at every unit direction. For any two parameter probabilities ρ₀,ρ₁, Vρ₀ is integrable under both laws. The actual scalar risk along (1−t)ρ₀+tρ₁ has right derivative ∫Vρ₀ dρ₁−∫Vρ₀ dρ₀ at zero, and F(ρ₁)≥F(ρ₀)+∫Vρ₀ dρ₁−∫Vρ₀ dρ₀.

items.statement: The adjacent complete statements, assumptions and formula proofs describe the exact generic results; the optional Lean is initially folded.
assumptions: E has finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel structures.
E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure; p is any finite real polynomial.
p is any finite real polynomial, including zero, constant and non-even polynomials. Weights form the literal unit-norm subtype.
ρ is any probability measure on the literal unit-norm subtype. No domination, moment, Bochner integrability or averaging identity is assumed.

formulae.label: Gaussian polynomial features vary continuously in L²
Scalar feature averages equal their Bochner L² means

obligations.label: Gaussian polynomial features vary continuously in L²
Scalar feature averages equal their Bochner L² means

bindings.boundary: This is a statement about actual standard Gaussian inputs, not every rotation-invariant or heavy-tailed law.; No parameter-law average, label, risk derivative, or spatial derivative is part of this continuity conclusion. The unit domain may be empty in dimension zero.

assumption_deltas.source: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure, γ its centered standard Gaussian law with identity covariance, and p any finite real polynomial. For every unit vector w, the actual scalar function x↦p(⟨w,x⟩) belongs to L²(γ). These membership witnesses can be chosen together so that their actual almost-everywhere equivalence classes form a continuous map from the unit sphere, with its subspace topology, into L²(γ). No feature moment, uniform bound, dominating function, or continuity assumption is supplied.

bindings.boundary: Pointwise evaluation is not treated as a continuous functional on L². The proof uses scalar Fubini and actual test-class inner products.; This averaging theorem has no label or risk derivative conclusion. In dimension zero there is no probability law on the empty unit subtype.

assumption_deltas.source: Under the same finite-dimensional real inner-product, Borel and finite-polynomial assumptions, let Φ(w) be the actual L² class of x↦p(⟨w,x⟩) under the standard Gaussian γ. The feature membership witnesses are produced together with continuity of Φ. For every probability law ρ on the unit sphere, the scalar feature is genuinely integrable in w for every fixed x, and Φ is genuinely Bochner integrable under ρ. The literal scalar-average function x↦∫p(⟨w,x⟩) dρ(w) belongs to L²(γ), and its actual L² class equals ∫Φ dρ. All membership, measurability and integral-exchange obligations are conclusions of the theorem.
